rightsRule: Only moments with rightsState=publishable and a verified asset may render. Research candidates never silently enter the public montage.

firstMoment.blocker: Archive.org exact MP4/OGV derivative URLs are resolved; binary redirect retrieval is blocked in the current execution environment. Frame verification remains mandatory.

researchState.discovery: Early-cinema catalogues reveal several distinct Entrée à Jérusalem productions, so the corpus can begin before 1903 rather than treating the Pathé 1902 tableau as the first screen representation.

earliestScreenLayer.finding: The corpus now reaches to Léar/Kirchner 1897 and Hatot/Lumière 1898 entry views. The homepage montage should begin with the earliest extant publishable moving image, not with an assumed 1903 origin.
earliestScreenLayer.gate: No production still may masquerade as a film Moment.

multiEraPass.finding: Verified representation line now spans 1897, 1898, 1902/03, 1912, 1927, 1961, 1965 and 1979. Discovery target is explicitly present-day, not a single early-cinema year.

modernEraPass.finding: The representation line now has verified anchors in 1993, 2014 and 2025. The current evidence span is 1897–2025, with discovery intentionally open beyond 2025.

rightsResearchPass.scope: public-domain-or-equivalently-permissive moving-image sources for the Entry into Jerusalem, searched through 2026
rightsResearchPass.conclusion: No additional post-1927 narrative Entry into Jerusalem film is admitted for public publication. Identity or online availability is not rights evidence.

candidates.admission: not admitted under the current public-domain-only rule

rightsResearchPass.nextSearch: Continue through 2026 for a rights-cleared contemporary commission, CC0 documentary material, or an explicit written license. Do not use material merely because a platform streams it.

artStillPass.finding: The moving-image montage now gains two intentionally brief painting intercuts: the 1873 Bible illustration cuts on palms/garments, and Morgner's 1912 expressionist entry resets procession scale. Both are verified public-domain reproductions from Wikimedia Commons.
artStillPass.rule: Paintings remain labelled assetType=image and animate only as short Ken Burns stills; they never represent unverified moving footage.

artHistoryPass.finding: The image layer now moves deliberately across 12th-century Georgian manuscript, early-14th-century Italian fresco, early-16th-century German woodcut, 19th-century Bible illustration and Doré, and 1912 Expressionism. Style changes are chronological acts of reception, not decorative interruptions.
artHistoryPass.admission: Every work is a verified Wikimedia Commons public-domain faithful reproduction.

artDensityPass.finding: The continuous film spine now receives eleven short historical exposures, distributed 2/2/2/2/2/1 across six six-second clips. Density grows without changing the moving-image duration.

montageScope.rule: Never stop the editorial montage at an arbitrary historical year. Continue discovery across silent, studio-epic, television, modern and contemporary screen eras. Rights admission remains per-Moment.

temporalBands.role: the biblical Moment appears almost with cinema itself
the tableau expands into feature-scale spectacle
mass crowd, widescreen and monumental Jerusalem
the entry becomes globally repeated screen memory
new cinematic, streaming and animated representations continue the recurrence

montageScope.editRule: Six moving-image clips carry the entire public rhythm. Each artwork is a single, low-opacity double exposure placed inside its paired clip; artwork neither consumes time nor introduces graphic framing.

stillEditingPass.reference: The documentary double-exposure treatment used to layer archival material with a live image: the historical picture is a temporal texture, never a card, caption, or replacement shot.
stillEditingPass.principle: Eleven historical images are paced as low-opacity double exposures across the six uninterrupted moving clips. Exposure density is distributed by action rather than by historical year, so the film carries the rhythm while the art creates a continuous visual undertow.

montageGrammarV2.principle: The six verified moving-image clips remain the uninterrupted spine. Each historical still now carries an explicit cut reason, focal point, virtual-camera path and exposure envelope; timing is still subordinate to the paired film action rather than decorative cadence.
rules: cut on biblical action or visual continuity, never merely on elapsed time
a still may push, pan, reframe or hold according to its composition
preserve moving film as temporal authority; stills are semantic counter-images
do not duplicate source-film frames in public playback
beauty gate evaluates the transition pair, not only each isolated frame
